# Scientific Context

The bundled source is from nmrglue, a Python package for reading, converting,
processing, and analyzing NMR spectroscopy data.

Reference:

Helmus, J. J. and Jaroniec, C. P. "Nmrglue: An open source Python package for
the analysis of multidimensional NMR data." Journal of Biomolecular NMR 55,
355-367 (2013). DOI: `10.1007/s10858-013-9718-x`.

Multidimensional NMR data are usually handled as arrays whose axes correspond to
direct and indirect time or frequency dimensions. In a fully sampled experiment,
the stored data naturally covers every indirect acquisition position. In a
compressed experiment, only selected positions are acquired, and the acquisition
record is part of the meaning of the dataset.

A processing library should therefore preserve enough layout information to
distinguish the stored stream from the multidimensional scientific object that
later processing expects. Downstream Fourier transforms, phasing, visualization,
and conversion routines depend on that dimensional meaning.
